look_here_first: Start with short, crowded racemes clustered into a tight windmill head. The decisive character is on a MATURE SPIKELET: the upper sterile lemma is rounded, swollen, hoodlike and about 1–1.5 mm; fertile and sterile awns are very short. A crowded head is a clue, not visual proof of the microscopic hood.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted POWO species and Texas state-level native distribution; source-pool admission approved; three target-zone county confirmations not independently verified.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial caespitose or tufted windmillgrass; Texas A&M notes occasional SHORT STOLONS, while an NRCS field account allows occasional short RHIZOMES. Whether any individual has connected runners must be proved by an actual rooted specimen, not assumed absent from a bunchgrass silhouette.
morphology_keys.spikelets: Fertile lemma ~1.5–2 mm with very short awn ~0.3–1.5 mm; sterile upper lemma swollen/hooded ~1–1.5 mm, awn absent or ≤1.5 mm.
best_field_traits: Inflated, rounded hood on the upper sterile lemma
Very short awns on both fertile and sterile florets
crew_field_walkthrough: Inspect the short crowded radiating branches on the flowering head, and photograph exactly where they arise.
Look at the dry hand-held specimen where individual spikelet-bearing branch segments are more distinct.
Isolate a mature spikelet under 10–20×: confirm swollen upper sterile lemma (roughly 1–1.5 mm), relatively short awns, and compare with a true C. verticillata specimen.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole mature flowering head with centimeter scale and crowding/whorl levels.
Dissected mature upper sterile lemma with rounded hood, front and side at millimeter scale.
Fertile lemma and separately measured short awn.
Matched head and awn photos of verticillata and any suspected hybrid.
morphology_keys.field_photo_limitations: The hood is a tiny upper sterile LEMMA, not a whole spikelet or visibly inflated green inflorescence; source determination kept provisional.
crew_field_steps: In the live head photograph, locate the very crowded shorter branches alongside longer spreading rays; photograph all tiers, not a cropped tuft.
The dried hand-held head photo shows individual one-sided branch spikelet rows more clearly. Mark only the actual photographed branch and spikelet rows.
For the hooded species ID, isolate one spikelet under 10–20× and measure the swollen rounded sterile lemma and its short awn. Neither current head photograph resolves the hood.

measured_reproductive_key_20261023.upper_glume_mm: 1–1.5 (Go Botany), versus 0.5–0.7 in Kew prose; requires voucher

comparisons.key_distinctions: Hooded windmillgrass generally has crowded shorter racemes (~2–5 cm) and a conspicuous rounded sterile hood with short awns. Tumble windmillgrass typically has longer (~5–15 cm) racemes in separated tiers and longer awns. Feather fingergrass commonly has a feathery terminal fan with long apical fertile-lemma hairs. The hybrid may be intermediate.
comparisons.cautions: Head color, overall windmill appearance and awn length alone can mislead. Inspect a fully mature spikelet with scale; hybrid intermediates must remain uncertain.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: How to identify Chloris cucullata in the field
steps: 1 · LIVING TEXAS HABIT: locally archived Jim Conrad Uvalde photograph is gallery panel 6; the newer Austin basal-foliage view is panel 11 and Cotulla attached flowering culm is panel 10. All show real growing structures, but none exposes connected roots or a measured inner ligule.

2 · WHOLE HEAD AND ONE-SIDED RACEMES: compare Fonseca's RIGHT-hand head (panel 0), Jim Conrad's Uvalde one-sided rows (panel 4), Tyler Cannon's Austin underside close-up (panel 9), and Cody Stricker's attached Cotulla head (panel 10). The unrelated dense LEFT plume in panel 0 must never be labelled this species.

3 · USDA SPIKELETS: Panel 2 already contains six original source-identified whole 1.5–2 mm spikelet units, a printed 2-mm bar, and rounded upper profiles. The new broad arrow indicates visible rounded profile ONLY, not the isolated upper sterile lemma.
4 · TEXAS CLOSEUP: Jim Conrad panel 3 shows real ciliate spikelet margins; his ripe panel 5 shows actual dark caryopses; neither dissects each glume, fertile lemma and sterile hood.

5 · FIELD DISSECTION: lift an authentic mature spikelet, expose separately the short-awed fertile lemma and the orbicular 1–1.5-mm upper sterile lemma in face and side, and retain two separately measured glumes beside 0.5-mm ruler.

6 · ROOT/COLLAR: since this perennial may sometimes have short stolons or rhizomes, show exposed roots and any connected rooting nodes; split the inner blade/sheath collar, photograph 0.7–1-mm ciliolate membrane with actual mm bar.

7 · LOOK-ALIKES AND PUBLIC QA: gallery panels 7 and 8 show OTHER species, C. verticillata and C. virgata. The 12-panel gallery contains 10 exact-species images and two look-alikes; verify all markers, licenses, source labels and mobile rendering. C. × subdolichostachya remains on taxonomic hold without measured mature floret evidence.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.LOOK HERE FIRST: Perennial 15–60 cm, many short 2–5 cm one-sided racemes clustered in close whorls; this is a field candidate, not species proof. Under 10–20× open one 1.5–2 mm spikelet: one fertile floret and one distal sterile floret; the upper sterile lemma is a rounded hood about 1–1.5 mm, unlike the longer-awned, well-separated tiers of C. verticillata.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form: Perennial, tufted (caespitose); erect culms 15–60 cm; leaf blades 2–4 mm wide; sheaths usually glabrous; no auricles documented in Go Botany.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.racemes: Kew GrassBase: about 10–20 unilateral racemes, 2–5 cm each, crowded in several close whorls; branch count is supporting only.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet: Kew and Go Botany: mature laterally flattened spikelet about 1.5–2 mm, with one fertile basal floret and one reduced distal sterile floret; distinguish spikelet length from each floret's lemma.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.lower_glume: Kew GrassBase lists 0.5–0.7 mm, one-veined and keeled; measure separately on a fully opened mature spikelet. Its internal length-ratio statement does not reconcile cleanly with its reported upper-glume length.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.upper_glume: Go Botany reports about 1–1.5 mm; Kew GrassBase's text separately gives 0.5–0.7 mm, creating a source discrepancy. Treat as a measurement requiring source-vouchered confirmation, NOT an absolute key threshold. Neither glume has a true long awn.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.fertile_lemma: Kew GrassBase: 1.5–2 mm, three-veined, ciliate along midvein and margins; principal subapical awn about 0.3–1.5 mm.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.upper_sterile_lemma: Kew GrassBase: one distal sterile floret with an orbicular, hoodlike lemma about 1–1.5 mm; sterile-lemma awn absent or up to about 1.5 mm. The hood is a lemma, NOT a swollen whole spikelet.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.ligule_and_collar: Go Botany: true ligule about 0.7–1 mm, a finely fringed membrane at the inner blade–sheath junction; distinguish from sheath surface hairs (typically absent). Photograph the free ligule edge with a 1-mm scale.
nearest_lookalikes: Chloris verticillata: flowering branches usually in distinctly separated tiers, and upper glumes about 2.8–3.5 mm in Go Botany; do not decide by tier spacing alone.
Chloris virgata: more feathery fan; conspicuous fertile-lemma apical hairs about 1.5–4 mm and fertile lemma awn about 5–15 mm in Kew GrassBase, unlike the short-awned hooded species.
Chloris × subdolichostachya: intermediate characters require verified parentage or specialist material; never infer hybrid identity from the same head silhouette.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Recognize short crowded one-sided windmill racemes; confirm a swollen upper sterile hood for final ID
field_id_short_tiles.details: Start with real Texas growing habit in panels 6 (Jim Conrad, Uvalde) and 11 (Don Bosan-Bruno, Austin). Panel 10 shows Cody Stricker's Cotulla flowering culm and its genuine slender stem carrying several short radiating terminal racemes; panel 9 is Tyler Cannon's close Austin view of dense one-sided spikelet rows. Older panels 4 and 1 show mature dried stage. Radiating heads alone are not species proof: the separate DENSE LEFT culm in panel 0 is not assigned to this species; only the right-hand one-sided head gets source-backed arrows. To confirm hooded windmillgrass against C. verticillata and hybrid look-alikes, observe the mature inflated UPPER STERILE lemma at about 1 mm scale.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE-LABELLED TX FLOWERING CULM / SHORT ONE-SIDED RACEMES / LIVING BASE PHOTOGRAPHED; STERILE HOOD UNDISSECTED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · CROWN AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Living ground-level tufts photographed twice; connected roots and true inner 1-mm ligule not yet shown
field_id_short_tiles.details: Use genuine target plants in panels 6 (Uvalde roadside), 11 (Austin narrow upright basal foliage), and 10 (Cotulla true slender attached flowering stem). These show growing tuft context, but the underground connected fibrous roots and any runners are HIDDEN, and nearby grasses in mixed vegetation may be other species. Texas A&M says short stolons sometimes occur, whereas NRCS also mentions short rhizomes; neither can be inferred here. The true ciliate MEMBRANOUS ligule is an INSIDE blade/sheath junction structure; no current photo opens it face-on beside a ruler. Do not mark an outer sheath edge, stem node or leaf hairs as that free membrane.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TWO REAL IN-GROUND HABIT PHOTOS PRESENT; EXPOSED ROOTS, ANY RUNNERS AND TRUE MEASURED INNER LIGULE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN ONE TINY SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: About 1.5–2 mm body; one fertile + one sterile floret
field_id_short_tiles.details: USDA's species-identified public-domain macro (panel 2) actually shows six WHOLE spikelet units and their rounded upper profiles beside a photographed 2-mm scale. They are not bare seeds. But the separately lifted upper sterile lemma is NOT yet individually proven. Jim Conrad's intact spikelets (panel 3) show marginal cilia, and his ripe raceme (panel 5) shows dark fruits. Mature spikelets are roughly 1.5–2 mm long, containing a lower fertile and small upper sterile floret; photograph one opened with 0.5-mm calibration. New panel 9 (Tyler Cannon) now shows actual Texas maturity-stage one-sided spikelet rows at closer range; it does not open the fertile vs sterile floret pair, isolate the glumes, or reveal the swollen upper sterile hood margin.
field_id_short_tiles.status: USDA TWO-MM WHOLE SPIKELETS PLUS ACTUAL AUSTIN ONE-SIDED ROWS; UPPER STERILE LEMMA STILL NOT ISOLATED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · KEEP GLUMES SEPARATE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Two basal glumes; upper-glume sources disagree
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase reports a lower glume about 0.5–0.7 mm; Go Botany reports an upper glume around 1–1.5 mm, while Kew's prose also gives 0.5–0.7 mm for the upper glume and inconsistent ratios. Preserve this disagreement: measure BOTH glumes separately on a vouchered mature specimen with 0.5-mm calibration. Neither glume is the hood or the source of a long lemma awn.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE GLUME DIMENSION CONFLICT RETAINED; 0.5-MM BACKLIT SEPARATED GLUMES NOT PHOTOGRAPHED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · HOOD AND SHORT AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Upper sterile lemma is a rounded 1–1.5 mm hood
field_id_short_tiles.details: In authentic USDA/Go Botany exact-species photographed spikelets (panel 2), rounded upper shapes resemble a hood, but these WHOLE units have not been dissected to reveal the actual upper STERILE lemma free margin. The lower fertile lemma is reportedly 1.5–2 mm with short awn about 0.3–1.5 mm; the upper reduced lemma is about 1–1.5 mm, swollen and rounded, with absent/short awn. The new arrow identifies only an upper rounded PROFILE, not a separately certified hood. A mature isolated same-voucher sterile lemma in TWO views beside 0.5-mm ruler remains essential.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL ROUNDED PROFILE ONLY; STERILE HOOD FREE MARGIN / TRUE SHORT AWN INSERTION UNPROVEN

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · WINDMILL LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Check mature florets, not only the head
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panels 7 and 8 are DIFFERENT taxa: tumble windmillgrass Chloris verticillata with longer tiered racemes/awns and feather fingergrass C. virgata with longer fertile-lemma hairs. Panel 6 is genuine live C. cucullata habit but not excavated. Hybrids C. × subdolichostachya may be intermediate; retain scientific hold until measured mature spikelets distinguish parentage. For true species closure, compare detached sterile hoods, both glumes and short fertile-lemma awns rather than head color. New source-vouchered Austin target raceme close-up (panel 9) teaches true gross spikelet arrangement, not the measured sterile-lemma hood needed to separate parent species from hybrids. Do not label mixed parents or hybrids by heads alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPARISON PANELS AVAILABLE; SAME-SCALE DISSECTIONS NEEDED
